page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors with a clock speed of up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. System memory is sized at 256 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with support for VNNI and BF16, alongside SHA, AES, and VAES cryptographic acceleration.

The D64as_v7 instance includes no bundled local disk storage and features zero integrated GPUs. Persistent storage requirements rely entirely on remote disk attachments via Azure Premium Storage interfaces. Memory subsystem throughput is measured at 206.82 GB/sec for large-block uncached read operations and 128.87 GB/sec for uncached write operations, complementing the processor cache architecture for data-dense pipelines.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational capabilities across integer, vector, and database processing. The processor achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests and PassMark database operations, reaching 34,994.2 operations. Single-threaded gzip compression performs in the top decile at 36.35 GB/sec. For memory-resident operations, the server delivers 94.83 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inferencing achieves top-tier throughput on smaller and medium-sized models, recording 4,242.19 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model and 44.43 tokens per second for generation on a 7B model.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the balanced vCPU-to-memory allocation maximizes resource utilization without paying a premium for idle local NVMe arrays or unused specialized accelerators. The primary operational tradeoff is the requirement for network-attached storage, which shifts I/O latency considerations to external storage tiers. D64as_v7 is suited for enterprise relational databases, Redis caching clusters, high-traffic web applications, continuous integration pipelines, and CPU-bound artificial intelligence inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D64as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors, providing 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores alongside 256 GB of system memory. Operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, the x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions, including VNNI and BF16, facilitating both high-throughput compute and accelerated inferencing tasks. Memory allocation follows a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU, supporting substantial in-memory operations and multi-threaded data processing. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote Premium Storage attachments for persistent file systems. Performance benchmarks show top-tier execution in single-core compute, database operations, and data compression, paired with strong memory bandwidth. D64as_v7 is tailored for enterprise backend services, distributed relational databases, static web serving fleets, continuous integration pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference workloads.
